mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts above 1200 thousand units signals strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1200.0, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in nonfarm payrolls signal robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, as measured by a negative Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0), manufacturing sector weakness signals potential economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 105.0, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL > 238.0) signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 238.0, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in less than 45% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average indicates strong consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS above its 3-month moving average fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5%), labor market slack suppresses wage growth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.5, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in less than 45% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signal broad-based economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, as measured by a Rank IC < -0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
